summary.name: Google SRE Production Services Best Practices
summary.one_liner: A free excerpt (Appendix B) from Google's Site Reliability Engineering book listing best practices for running production services, covering failure handling, rollouts, SLOs, error budgets, monitoring, postmortems, capacity planning, overload, and on-call staffing.
use_cases: Designing alerting so only actionable issues page on-call engineers
Planning staged rollouts of config or binary changes
Setting SLOs and error budgets for a service
Handling overload with load shedding and backoff
Sizing on-call teams and limiting operational toil
summary.what_it_does: The page is an excerpt from Google's free SRE book covering a collection of operating principles for production services. It recommends validating configuration inputs and keeping the previous state when new input looks wrong, rolling out changes in stages across traffic fractions and geographies, and measuring availability from the end user's perspective. It describes error budgets as 1 minus the SLO, with a freeze on launches when the budget is spent. It also covers monitoring output types (pages, tickets, logging), blameless postmortems, N+2 capacity planning, graceful overload handling with exponential backoff, and on-call team sizing with a 50% toil limit. Examples include a 2005 DNS empty-file outage and a 2009 malware-flagging incident.
notable: Excerpt from Google's free Site Reliability Engineering book
Includes real incident examples such as the 2005 DNS empty-file outage and 2009 malware-flagging config error
Describes error budgets and SLOs measured at the client rather than the server
Recommends N+2 capacity provisioning and minimum on-call team sizes
caveats: Describes general practices rather than a software tool; no product features or downloads
Recommendations reflect Google's scale and may not fit smaller teams without adaptation
